newsitem.title: JAPAN: Shipping shares fall on Japan-U.S. port dispute.
newsitem.headline: Shipping shares fall on Japan-U.S. port dispute.

text.p: Shares in the shipping sector fell on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE) on Friday morning due to the bilateral dispute between Japan and the United States over port practices, traders said.
By 0125 GMT, shares in the sector were down 2.51 percent, making it the largest loser of any industrial sector on the TSE.
Nippon Yusen KK fell 13 yen to 467 at midday, and Mitsui O.S.K. Lines Ltd was down 10 yen at 239. Kawasaki Kisen Kaisha Ltd was down 13 yen at 235.

The U.S. Federal Maritime Commission (FMC) said on Wednesday that it would slap $100,000 surcharges on Japanese vessels calling at U.S. ports in retaliation for what it termed "unfavourable restrictive practices". The commission said the surcharges would become effective on April 14.

The FMC said the surcharges would be imposed each time a vessel owned or operated by Kawasaki Kisen, Mitsui O.S.K. Lines or Nippon Yusen entered a U.S. port from abroad, but not from another U.S. port.
The Japanese government on Thursday strongly urged the U.S. to withdraw its threat of sanctions and warned that the row could harm overall bilateral ties.
